channel.title: FZ1073 Incident Monitor (EN)
channel.description: Running overview of public information on the flydubai FZ1073 incident (30 Sep 2026). Distinguishes official, data, media and unconfirmed reports.

item.title: [Media] Saudi Gazette: Saudi NTSC opens safety investigation into Tabuk landing (clarifies u025)
item.description: [Media] According to the directly read Saudi Gazette article, the Saudi National Transport Safety Center said it received a report of the incident and sent an investigation team to establish circumstances and evidence from an aviation-safety perspective. The article also says the UAE runs a separate criminal investigation led by the Attorney General, to examine motives and any link to terrorism. This is a retelling of agency reporting; the center's own statement was not read directly. (Source: Saudi Gazette)

item.title: [Official] UAE MoFA: monitoring FZ1073 incident, Attorney General ordered investigation
item.description: [Official] The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs (text read directly via WebFetch) says it is monitoring the incident and that the Attorney General ordered an investigation team. It states UAE law applies to the UAE-registered aircraft even outside UAE territory, and the probe is to cover possible terrorism links, planning or external direction. It urges the public to rely only on official sources. (Source: Ministerstvo zahraničních věcí SAE (MoFA))

item.title: [Media] Arab News: UAE probe to assess terrorism; captain opened cockpit door
item.description: [Media] Arab News (article read directly) says the attacker was an Omani national and the injured captain opened the cockpit door, allowing passengers to restrain the attacker; 174 people were aboard. The UAE probe is to determine whether it was terrorism or planned, Netanyahu reportedly said it is too early to say who is behind it, and India's prime minister called the pilot a hero. These are media-relayed claims; nationality and sequence are not verified by authorities. (Source: Arab News)

item.title: [Media] CNN: suspect expected to be handed to UAE, axe weapon unconfirmed, Ben Gvir demands extradition to Israel
item.description: [Media] CNN (live blog read directly) quotes Israeli PM Netanyahu: the suspect was detained by Saudi authorities and Netanyahu expects him to be transferred to the UAE for questioning with Israeli involvement; he called the use of an axe unconfirmed. An Israeli official told CNN the first officer had worked at flydubai for eight months. Minister Ben Gvir demands the suspect be extradited to Israel; the UAE bases jurisdiction on the aircraft's registration. These are claims by Israeli officials relayed by the media, not verified investigation findings. (Source: CNN)

item.title: [Media] UAE Attorney-General orders investigation team for FZ1073
item.description: [Media] According to a Dubai Eye article (read directly), the UAE Attorney-General ordered a Public Prosecution team to establish the motives of the incident and assess possible premeditation or terrorist links, in coordination with the GCAA. The UAE bases jurisdiction on the aircraft being UAE-registered. The Attorney-General urged the public not to spread speculation. The statement text itself was not read on an official site. (Source: Dubai Eye 103.8)

item.title: [Media] CNN: Israel calls it a terror attack, motive unconfirmed; El Al preparing evacuation flights from Dubai
item.description: [Media] CNN (live blog read directly) says Israel calls the incident an attempted terrorist attack, but no motive is confirmed and the attacker has not been officially identified; one Israeli official says he is an Omani national. CNN reports the plane fell 17,400 ft in under two minutes (conflicts with FR24's >14,000 ft in <30 s). El Al is preparing to evacuate Israelis from Dubai, no date set; flydubai operated about 70 flights a week on the route. (Source: CNN)

item.title: [Media] Newsweek: Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia says captain's condition is stable
item.description: [Media] According to Newsweek (article read directly), citing AP, the Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia said the captain is in stable condition; Israeli media reportedly write of surgery for his wounds. This is relayed information not verified by the maintainer; no official medical report was found. (Source: Newsweek (přes AP))

item.title: [Media] Emirates suspends codeshare flights with flydubai to Tel Aviv
item.description: [Media] According to Gulf News (article read directly), Emirates has suspended its codeshare operations with flydubai to and from Tel Aviv with immediate effect until further notice. Passengers whose final destination is Tel Aviv will not be accepted at their origin; those already en route will be supported to complete their journeys. Khaleej Times reports the same (search results only). (Source: Gulf News)

item.title: [Media] ABC: Netanyahu praises injured captain, cause still unknown per flydubai
item.description: [Media] According to ABC (article read directly), the Israeli prime minister claims the injured captain opened the cockpit door, which let passengers and crew overpower the attacker. ABC says flydubai states the underlying reasons remain unknown and warns against premature conclusions. ABC also reports that Saudi Arabia arrested one pilot and that it is unexplained how a weapon got on board; these are claims by Israeli officials and media, not official investigation findings, and no lead investigating authority has published any yet. (Source: ABC News (Australia))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Saudi national transport safety centre opens investigation into Tabuk landing
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to search results (page not read directly, site returns 403), Saudi outlet Sabq reports that the national transport safety centre has opened an investigation into the FZ1073 emergency landing at Tabuk and an investigation team has begun work with the relevant authorities. No directly read statement from the centre confirms this yet; the relationship to the GCAA UAE investigation is not specified. (Source: Sabq (přes vyhledávání))

item.title: [Media] Al Jazeera: FZ1073 timeline, attack claim not independently confirmed
item.description: [Media] According to Al Jazeera (read directly), unusual manoeuvres began at 05:21Z, squawk 7700 at 05:28Z and 7500 at 05:35Z, landing in Tabuk at 06:45Z. The outlet describes Netanyahu's claim of a pilot stabbing and attempt to crash the aircraft as not independently confirmed, as is the Omani nationality of the other pilot. Squawk times differ slightly from other sources (05:31Z / 05:38Z), and the opposition (Lapid) questions political use of the incident. (Source: Al Jazeera)

item.title: [Official] flydubai (official site): cockpit altercation and suspension of Israel flights
item.description: [Official] The flydubai official website (read directly) carries three statements: the aircraft landed safely in Tabuk, an altercation occurred in the flight deck and was contained by the crew, and all passengers and crew are safe. The carrier is suspending flights to and from Israel in coordination with authorities while the investigation continues. This confirms earlier reports (u010, u022); it gives no cause or identities. (Source: flydubai News)

item.title: [Unconfirmed] flydubai temporarily suspends all flights to and from Israel
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to a Dubai Eye article (read directly; the flydubai statement on its own website has not yet been read directly), the carrier temporarily suspended all flights to and from Israel in coordination with the relevant authorities so the FZ1073 investigation can continue. It apologised to affected passengers and said it would review the suspension as more information emerges. (Source: Dubai Eye 103.8)

item.title: [Media] GCAA UAE: 'security incident' on FZ1073 brought under control, crew members injured
item.description: [Media] According to Gulf News (read directly), the UAE GCAA said flight FZ1073 experienced a security incident that was brought under control, and the aircraft made an emergency landing at Tabuk. Some crew members were injured and treated at a Saudi hospital; GCAA investigation teams are working with relevant authorities on causes and circumstances. The statement text on the GCAA website itself was not read directly (the page contained nothing on it), so this is a media report, not status official; it is the first GCAA statement found on the incident. (Source: Gulf News (cituje prohlášení GCAA UAE))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] New onboard videos and photos from Tabuk
item.description:
[Unconfirmed] Media have published more footage: a passenger's video shortly before landing, a video of passengers intervening and a cabin video during the descent (shared on X), a photo of passengers disembarking in Tabuk and, per search results, photos of the damaged rudder (Times of Israel; page not read directly). The directly read One Mile at a Time also mentions rudder damage; it is not officially confirmed (see u006). No one has officially verified the origin or authenticity of the footage; some videos may be graphic. (Source: Israel National News / The Media Line / One Mile at a Time / The Daily Telegraph / Times of Israel)
Video: Passenger films the situation after the attacker was subdued, shortly before landing in Tabuk (unverified) (autor ve zdroji neuveden (via Israel National News), via Israel National News / The Media Line / One Mile at a Time / The Daily Telegraph / Times of Israel)
Video: Onboard video: passengers intervene (The Daily Telegraph, YouTube Shorts; unverified) (The Daily Telegraph (AU), via Israel National News / The Media Line / One Mile at a Time / The Daily Telegraph / Times of Israel)
Video: Cabin video during the steep descent, screaming audible (shared on X, original author unknown; unverified) (Heidi Bachram (@HeidiBachram) na X, původní autor neuveden, via Israel National News / The Media Line / One Mile at a Time / The Daily Telegraph / Times of Israel)
Photo: Passengers disembark in Tabuk (lead photo of The Media Line article; unverified) (sociální sítě (dle popisku The Media Line), via Israel National News / The Media Line / One Mile at a Time / The Daily Telegraph / Times of Israel)
Photo: Photos of the tail after landing – damaged rudder (Times of Israel, per search results; unverified) (autor ve zdroji neuveden, via Israel National News / The Media Line / One Mile at a Time / The Daily Telegraph / Times of Israel)

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Media: two off-duty pilots travelling as passengers reportedly broke into the cockpit
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to search results (pages not read directly), media reportedly say two off-duty pilots travelling as passengers (one South African, one from New Zealand) got into the cockpit with help from cabin crew and passengers and restrained the other pilot. These are individual websites, not confirmed by authorities or flydubai; one search also cites a descent from FL340 to about 19,000 ft in ~90 s, yet another variant among the conflicting descent profiles. (Source: Newsweek / Migflug / Cedar News (přes vyhledávání))

item.title: [Media] Tabuk Airport: all passengers departed on a replacement aircraft, both pilots in hospital
item.description: [Media] According to Saudi Gazette (article read directly), Tabuk airport says the distress call came at 08:44 local time, the aircraft landed at 09:45 and all passengers left on a replacement aircraft at 17:40. Both the captain and the co-pilot were injured and taken to hospital; the airport says the competent authorities are investigating. The article also repeats flydubai's statement that causes and motives are unknown. (Source: Saudi Gazette)

item.title: [Media] Israeli Defense Minister Katz: attempted terrorist attack; flydubai urges no speculation
item.description: [Media] According to Ynetnews (article read directly), Defense Minister Katz called the incident an attempted "jihadist terrorist attack" and said the intent was to crash the aircraft; this is a claim by an Israeli official, not a confirmed fact. Flydubai, by contrast, says the causes and motives are unknown and subject to an official investigation, and urges against speculation. Israeli passengers left Tabuk on a replacement flight after Mossad vetted the crew. (Source: Ynetnews)

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Second flydubai flight to Tel Aviv: media say tracking glitch
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to search results (pages not read directly), hours after FZ1073 reports emerged that another flydubai flight was turning back from Tel Aviv. Media say it was a glitch on flight-tracking sites and flight FZ1081 continued normally; there is no official confirmation. (Source: The Week / Business Today / Cedar News (přes vyhledávání))

item.title: [Media] Netanyahu: pilot stabbed the other and was arrested by the Saudis
item.description: [Media] According to search results (JPost, AFP and others; pages not read directly), Israeli PM Netanyahu said one pilot stabbed the other, apparently tried to crash the plane or sabotage its systems, and was arrested and is being questioned by Saudi authorities. This is a claim by the Israeli side; UAE/KSA and investigators have not officially confirmed it, and it conflicts with the AvHerald headline (u014) about a suspected suicide attempt. (Source: Jerusalem Post / AFP / další (přes vyhledávání))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] AvHerald updates headline: F/O under investigation for suspected suicide attempt
item.description: [Unconfirmed] At 09:59Z AvHerald changed its article headline to “first officer under investigation for suspected suicide attempt” (previously only “fight in the cockpit”). Only the headline on AvHerald's official Bluesky account was read directly, not the article itself – who is leading the investigation and what the headline is based on is unknown. This contradicts the Israeli assessment of a possible terrorist act; none of it is officially confirmed. Supplements u009. (Source: The Aviation Herald (titulek na Bluesky @avherald.com))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Israel: joint investigation, origin of pilots' passports also examined
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to search results (pages not read directly), Mossad, Shin Bet, the military and the transport ministry are involved in the investigation in Israel, which assesses the incident as a possible terror attack. Israeli media say the first officer had worked at flydubai for about nine months, and the transport minister has asked for a check of compliance with agreements on pilots holding passports of states with diplomatic ties to Israel; none of this is officially confirmed. (Source: Israel Hayom / Kan / Reuters (přes vyhledávání))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Conflict: captain's nationality – Indian vs. Emirati
item.description: [Unconfirmed] Indian media, according to search results (pages not read directly) and citing Israeli sources, say the captain is Indian. This contradicts entry u011, where an Israeli official (via CNN) described the captain as a UAE citizen. Neither claim has been officially confirmed. (Source: The Week / India TV (přes vyhledávání))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Israeli official: captain from the UAE, second pilot from Oman; media describe stab wound
item.description: [Unconfirmed] Media citing an Israeli official say the captain is a UAE national and the second pilot an Omani national, and that it is suspected the second pilot tried to crash the aircraft. Some reports mention a stab wound to the captain and two off-duty pilots among the passengers who helped; none of this is officially confirmed and details differ from earlier reports. Content was not read directly. (Source: CNN / Reuters (přes vyhledávání))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] flydubai: emergency caused by altercation between pilots, investigation opened
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to search results (the carrier's page was not read directly) flydubai says the emergency signal was triggered by a violent altercation between the pilots, the aircraft landed safely in Tabuk and passengers are fine. The carrier reportedly opened its own investigation and sent a replacement aircraft to Tabuk. (Source: flydubai (news.flydubai.com))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] AvHerald and ASN have an entry – content not available for automated reading
item.description: [Unconfirmed] Both sites block automated access, so the monitor only picks up changes to these entries indirectly (via search). (Source: The Aviation Herald / ASN)

item.title: [Media] Euronews: Israeli officials speak of an averted disaster
item.description: [Media] Summary of witness accounts of one pilot being stabbed and the Israeli suspicion of a terrorist act. (Source: Euronews)

item.title: [Media] Video: injured passenger's account
item.description:
[Media] Video of a passenger describing the attack in the cockpit. The video content has not been verified; the source is an aggregator. (Source: Cedar News)
Video: passenger's account (via Cedar News)

item.title: [Media] Tabuk airport: both pilots injured; Israel asks to halt flydubai flights
item.description:
[Media] JPost cites a Tabuk airport statement that both pilots were injured and taken to hospital. Transport Minister M. Regev asked Shin Bet to suspend flydubai flights. It also mentions a photo of a damaged rudder – not technically verified, unconfirmed. (Source: Jerusalem Post)
Photo: damaged rudder per JPost (unconfirmed) (autor ve zdroji neuveden, via Jerusalem Post)

item.title: [Media] Passenger describes subduing the attacker in the cockpit
item.description: [Media] A passenger (CEO of Barak Capital Underwriting) says he entered the cockpit with other men and a relief pilot and overpowered the attacker. This is a witness account, not an investigation finding. (Source: Ctech (Calcalist))

item.title: [Media] Israel: suspicion the F/O tried to crash the aircraft
item.description:
[Media] According to the Israeli assessment the F/O (reportedly from Oman) is the suspect. Contact with Saudi Arabia is handled by Mossad. Ynet says flydubai described the incident as a scuffle between pilots and opened its own investigation – that statement is not yet visible in other sources. (Source: Ynetnews)
Photo: illustrative flydubai photo (2024), not from the incident (Photofex_AUT / Shutterstock.com, via Ynetnews)

item.title: [Media] Israeli sources: not a hijacking
item.description: [Media] Early Israeli reports ruled out a hijacking; the explanation was said to be a cockpit altercation. No statement in the flydubai newsroom at that time. Ynet: 174 PAX incl. 27 children; the aircraft briefly entered Jordanian airspace and turned back. (Source: AeroCorner)

item.title: [Data] FR24: flight ADS-B data, squawk 7700 → 7500 → 7700
item.description:
[Data] Departure 03:05Z, FL340, last ADS-B 06:58Z after landing in Tabuk. The blog offers a CSV with barometric altitude, GS and vertical speed – useful for your own analysis of the descent profile. (Source: Flightradar24 blog)
Photo: FR24 extended timeline (X) (Flightradar24 (@flightradar24), via Flightradar24 blog)
Video: FR24 flight playback (Flightradar24, via Flightradar24 blog)

item.title: [Official] flydubai confirms incident and safe landing in Tabuk
item.description:
[Official] A flydubai spokesperson confirmed an incident on FZ1073 DXB–TLV, a safe landing at TUU and that all passengers are fine. No cause given. The article cites KAN on a 'fight between pilots' – per AeroTime not independently confirmed. (Source: AeroTime)
Photo: illustrative flydubai B38M (not A6-FKF) (Markus Mainka / Shutterstock.com, via AeroTime)
Photo: FR24 timeline (X) (Flightradar24 (@flightradar24), via AeroTime)
